1.

By this award, the claim petition bearing MACP No.188/19 seeking compensation under Sections 166 (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the accident, based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) would be decided.

2. Briefly stated facts as per the FIR are that on 29.08.2017 at about 6:50 pm, the petitioner was coming back to her house at Arawali Apartment, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. from her office via National Highway-24, Ghazipur, Delhi on her scooty bearing registration No DL-7SBD-9244.

It is further stated that the petitioner took turn from flyover circle of Ghazipur Murga Mandi towards EDM Mall, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. and at that time, two hydra cranes bearing registration No.
Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
1 HR-55V-4780 and HR-99XBT-4138 were carrying a big stone without following the public safety and safeguards or blocking of the road there.

While the petitioner passed by therefrom, one crane bearing registration No HR-55V-4780 came over the petitioner, as a result of which, petitioner fell down on road alongside her scooty and weight loading part of the crane fell down over the right hand of the petitioner and smashed her right hand.
FIR bearing no. 313/17 PS- Ghazipur, was registered in connection with the accident.

3. In response to the notice of the petition, all the respondents appeared and filed their replies /
written statements.

3(i). In the joint written statement filed by respondent Nos. 1 & 2 (in the capacity of the owner and driver respectively of Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-99XBT-4138), they have asserted that no accident has even been committed by the respondent No.2 at any point of time with Crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 and police has falsely implicated the respondent No. 1 & 2 in the present matter.
It is further averred that said vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident.
It is further asserted that police officials of PS Ghazipur have obtained the signatures of the respondents on blank papers in the police station.
It is further averred that the investigating officer has not conducted a fair investigation.
It is further stated that respondents are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
It is further stated that the respondent No. 2 had a valid driving licence.

In the separate written statement filed by R1 (in the capacity of the owner-cum-driver of Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780), it is stated that no accident has been committed at any point of time with the alleged vehicle bearing No.HR-55V-4780.

It is further stated that police has falsely implicated R1 and he is not liable to pay any compensation and further that the said crane was duly insured on the date of accident and having other relevant documents i.e. fitness, permit, RC etc. and further that R1 had a valid driving licence.

Respondent No.3 / insurer has filed its written statement and has taken defence that the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 was not holding any valid driving licence on the date of accident for driving the class of vehicle involved in the accident.
It is further stated that crane bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 was not having any valid permit and fitness certificate for use in the present case.

It is stated that the permit was valid only for Haryana and the fitness was valid upto 02.03.2017, whereas the accident took place on 29.08.2017 and thus terms and conditions of the insurance policy have been willfully violated by the insured.

It is further stated that owner and insurer of crane bearing registration No.
HR-99XBT-4138 have not been made a party nor any document of the said vehicle has been filed in the DAR.

It is further stated that as per DAR, the concrete slab slipped from HR-99XBT-4138 due to the negligence of Respondent No.2/Satender and due to the load of the slab, the other crane bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 toppled, falling on the injured and thus the negligence was solely of the crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138.

It is further averred that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 was not responsible for the alleged accident, which was caused due to the sole negligence of the crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138.
4.
On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 06.06.2019:-

(i) Whether the petitioner Kriti Kishore suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident which happened on 29.08.2017 at about 6:50 p.m. near Gabbar Construction Company office, Sabzi Mandi Road Ghazipur, Delhi, within jurisdiction of PS Ghazi pur, due to rash and negligent driving of hydra cranes bearing Registration Nos. HR-55V-4780 and HR-99XBT-4438, driven by respondent No.1 /
Nand Kishore and respondent No.2 / Satender Singh respectively ?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of the said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP)
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

(OPP) 
(iv)Relief.
5. In order to establish her claim, petitioner examined three witnesses.

5(i). Petitioner / PW1 deposed on the strength of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and deposed regarding manner of accident, injuries suffered by her and the medical expenses incurred on her treatment and relied upon the following documents:-
Photocopy of driving licence and aadhar card of petitioner are Ex.PW1/1 (colly,2 sheets) (OSR)

Photocopies of bank passbook of the petitioner is Ex. PW1/7 5(ii).

PW2 Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir, Specialist Orthopedics, LBS Hospital, Khichripur, Delhi proved the disability certificate as Ex.
PW2/A mentioning 93% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb.
Copy of assessment sheet is Ex.PW2/B. 5(iii).
PW3, Sh. Akash Singh, Sr. Executive, Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi produced the treatment record of the petitioner and proved three discharge summaries of the petitioner Ex. PW3/A to Ex. PW3/C.
Further, he also proved three final bills of the Max Hospital Ex.PW3/D, Ex. PW3/E and Ex. PW3/F.
Petitioner was cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for respondents.
6. Respondent No.1 and Respondent No. 3 / insurer opted to lead evidence in their defence.

6(i). Respondent No.1 has stepped into witness box as R1W1.
6(ii). R-3 / insurer has examined Ms. Sunidhi Mittal, Nodal Officer of the IFFCO Tokio General Insurance company as R3W1 in its defence.

R3W1 has relied upon the following documents :-

3  Copy of insurance policy i.e. Ex.R1W1/R2  Notice under order XII Rule 8 CPC issued to the respondents i.e. Ex.R1W1/R1 7.
I have heard Sh. Ramanand Chaudhary and Sh. Rajesh Goel, Ld. Counsel for R3/Insurer.

Opportunity of R-1 and R-2 to address arguments was closed, as none appeared on behalf of R-1 and R-2.
8.

The issues are decided as follows:-
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
10. Now in this case, the petitioner Kriti @ Krity Kishore is injured and eye witness of the accident.
In order to establish her claim, she has examined herself as PW-1.

She stated on oath in the affidavit that on 29.08.2017 at about 6:50 pm, when she was coming back to her house at Aravali Apartment,
Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. from her office via National Highway-24, Ghazipur, Delhi on her scooty bearing registration No. Dl-7SBD-9244 and when she took turn from flyover circle of Ghazipur, Murgamandi towards EDM Mall, at that time, two hydra cranes bearing Registration No.HR-55V-4780 and HR-99X-BT4138 were carrying a big stone without following public safety safeguards or blocking of the road and traffic was coming and going.

Petitioner passed from there and at that time, crane bearing No. HR-55V-4780 came over the petitioner, due to which, petitioner fell down on the road and the weight loading part of the crane fell down on right hand of the petitioner.
Petitioner saw that the crane was in fallen down condition and the registration number of the crane which had fallen down on the right hand of the petitioner was HR-55V-4780.
R1/driver of the Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780 examined himself in defence as R1W1.
He deposed in his cross-examination, admitting that his crane HR-55V-4780 had toppled and fallen down on the petitioner.
He also deposed that the contents of the FIR are wrong and that only one crane was carrying the slab.
He also disclosed that he is not aware what statement had been given by Rati Ram under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

Rati Ram is cited in the charge-sheet as an eye-witness but he was not examined either by the petitioner or by any of the respondents and hence, his version did not come on record during enquiry made by Tribunal.

His statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has purpose only to the extent of cross-examination to contradict him during his testimony before the Tribunal by putting his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. to him, if there is any contradiciton in his version.
In the absence of his examination before the Tribunal, his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C which is part of charge-sheet attached to the DAR- has no significance.

Further, a perusal of the statement of this witness under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
reflects that what he had stated to Police was that hydra crane yellow colour was bringing a concrete floor (iron contained) lying on road towards godown.
He further stated that suddenly hook of one of the hydra cranes broke and came out, due to which balance of that crane got disturbed, which was moving towards NH-24 and being driven on back side.

The crane toppled and a big portion of the Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
4 hydra crane fell over the petitioner.
This statement in itself is nowhere.

It does not clarify as to which of the cranes had toppled and does not at all suggest that one of the cranes toppled, while hook of another was broken and fell on another, as suggested by Ld. Counsel for R3/Insurer of vehicle bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780.
The black and white copies of photographs also do not show anything to suggest regarding involvement and negligence of hydra crane number HR-99-XBT-4138 in the accident.

Hence, on the basis of testimonies and materials on record, it can fairly be said that the accident took place due to rash and negligent conduct of the driver-cum-owner of the hydra crane bearing No. HR-55V-4780/R1 Nand Kishore.

As far as R2 is concerned, none of the parties led any evidence which could point out even prima-facie regarding involvement of the said crane in the accident, regardless of the fact whether the said crane was being driven and was in motion at the time of accident and being driven without taking necessary precaution of cordoning off the site of the operation.

In the absence of anything to suggest that while acting in tandem during carrying of the slab together fastened onto their lifting parts, hydra crane bearing No.
HR-99X-BT4138 was operated in such a manner as resulting in the losing of balance by the hydra crane HR-55V-4780, it cannot automatically be deduced that the driver of the said crane attributed to the accident by any of his rash or negligent conduct.
FIR was registered in the present case on same day i.e. date of accident.
During her cross-examination, petitioner denied that crane number HR-99X-BT4138 had toppled and fallen down.
She also denied that guard at the spot had warned her and there was a safety tap fixed at the construction site.

No photographs of the site of accident is filed to show that it was a well cordoned off area with all safety precautions taken and that petitioner breached such security and deliberately managed to enter the area.
PW1 remained consistent during her cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for respondents.
MLC of the petitioner was prepared on the same day and reflects the alleged history of road traffic accident.

The mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780 shows fresh damages on the same and clearly mentions that apart from the damages on its body, the front towing hook / steel lift wire attached to the towing hook was found damaged and that the vehicle was found off road.
R1 has not disputed that he was driver-cum-owner of hydra crane HR-55V-4780 at the date and time of accident or that the same had toppled over.
He did not disclose the reason for toppling over of the said hydra crane and kept mum in this regard in his testimony.
It is relevant here to note that no suggestion was given to R1W1 to show the involvement and fault of the other crane resulting in toppling of crane driven by R1W1.

Even though, Ld. Counsel for insurer argued during final arguments that hook of the other crane had broken and fallen over the crane No. HR-55V-4780,
resulting in the same losing balance and falling on the petitioner, the documents on record do not suggest so.

The medical documents of the petitioner together with her testimony reflect that she sustained grievous injuries in the accident due to part of crane No. HR-55V-4780 falling down on her and same having toppled over.
11. After investigation, police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1/ the driver of the offending vehicle i.e Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
No evidence was led by any of the respondents in their defence and R1 did not enter into witness box to assail the claim of the petitioner.
13. Respondent no.1 and 3 did not lead any cogent evidence to assail the claim of the petitioner.
R-1 admitted the factum of accident in his testimony and that charge-sheet was filed against him.
He also admitted that he had not filed any complaint to any competent authority regarding his false implication.

He also admitted in his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for R3/Insurer that the hydra crane HR-55V-4780 did not have fitness certificate on the date of accident and further that he did not produce the permit qua the said crane.

R3 did not lead any evidence on the point of involvement of R2 in causing of the accident or him attributing to the accident or on the point of contributory negligence by driver of Hydra Crane No. HR-99-XBT-4138 i.e. Satender Singh Yadav.

Even though R2 is charge-sheeted in the case FIR No. 313/17 PS Ghazipur under section 270/ 287/ 338 IPC,
adverse conclusion cannot be drawn against him of rash and negligent driving as resulting in injuries to the petitioner, in absence of any evidence led in this regard.
Insurance company did not even chose to examine IO to show any negligent conduct of R-2 as resulting in the accident in question and having any direct bearing on sustaining of injuries by her.

14. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1/ Nand Kishore, the driver-cum-owner of the hydra crane bearing Registration No HR-55V-4780.

Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondent nos. 1 & 3 but in favour of Respondent No.2.
ISSUE No.2:
15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
6 and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though she may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.

17. Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to her under the afore-said heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
18.
Petitioner has placed on record medical bills (part of document Ex.PW1/H).

The document Ex.
PW1/H consists of treatment record of Yashoda Hospital as well as Max Healthcare and medical bills of Max Healthcare and certain pharmacy bills to the tune of Rs.13,03,640/- (apart from the reimbursed amount).
This amount includes certain physiotherapy bills of the petitioner.

( amount of physiotherapy bill No. 015 dated 31.07.2018 for the period from 07.06.2018 to 31.07.2018 is mentioned at second last serial number of break up of medical bills as Rs.30,000/-, whereas the same is of Rs.21,000/-).
Further, bill at Serial No. 33 and 35 are in duplication in the break up.

Further, in final bill No. PG-1C301196 of Max Healthcare, it is specified that an amount of Rs.2,78,500/- was reimbursed by the insurance company and further total discount of Rs. 21,498/-
was given to the petitioner in the final bill of 11,88,677/-.

Ld. Counsel for insurance company submitted that the amount paid by the TPA/ medical insurance need not to be paid to the petitioner under this head whereas, Ld. Counsel for petitioner staked claim to this amount on ground that premium was paid by the petitioner and further contract with medical insurance company is separate and insurance company cannot get benefit out of it.

In this regard, petitioner has relied on judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court bearing citation Royal Sundaram Alliance Company Ltd.
Vs. Mr. Ajit Chandrakant Rakvi & Anr. FA No.1620 of 2012, decided on 19.03.2019.
Further, I have gonethrough the citations

United India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Patrica Jean Mahajan & Ors. of Supreme Court of India in Appeal (Civil) 3655-58 of 2002; and Mrs. Helen C. Rebello & Ors. Vs.
Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation of Supreme Court of India decided on 18.09.1998.

Under this head, only original medical bills/expenses are to be considered.

Hence, a sum of Rs.15,82,140/- (Rs.13,03,640/- +
Rs.2,78,500) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

7
PAIN AND SUFFERING:

19. According to her affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was first taken to Yashoda Hospital, Kaushambi Ghaizabad, and thereafter shifted to Max Hospital, Patparganj,
Delhi.

Her right hand elbow was operated upon and injury of the petitioner was diagnosed as crush injury right elbow with fracture, dislocation near total amputation with right distil ulna fracture with crush injury right index finger with right ILIAC wing fracture.

In her affidavit attested on 31.01.2018, she stated that she could not recover and is having same problem in her right hand and further that she was on bed and her repeated dressing were being done at the hospital with no improvement shown and further that she was unable to resume her job.
OPD consultation of Max hospital shows that she visited the hospital for treatment at least till 27.11.2017.
The bill summary of Yashoda Hospital reflects that she was admitted there on 29.08.2017 and thereafter discharged on the same day.
Further, the duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted to the hospital on 29.08.2017 and discharged on 15.09.2017.
Further, another duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted on 19.09.2017 and discharged on 23.09.2017.
Further, another duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted for the third time in the said hospital on 16.11.2017 and discharged on same after wound was repaired.

Hence, it cannot be ignored that petitioner suffered grievous injuries and further near total amputation of right upper limb and she must have been in a bad condition after the accident and must have remained on bed for a long period of time.
She must have endured immense pain and difficulty in her day to day life.

In these circumstances,
considering the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.
3,00,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 20.
In her examination in chief, PW1 / petitioner has not averred anything regarding the expenses on conveyance, special diet and attendant charges.
She has not proved any actual expenses in relation to conveyance, special diet and attendant charges.
Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and period of treatment, I deem it fit to grant Rs.30,000/- to petitioner for conveyance.

Though no document has been placed on record by the petitioner to suggest that she has spent any sum of Rs.1,00,000/- on special diet as claimed in the written arguments, still considering the nature of injuries and hospitalization of the petitioner, it can be assumed that petitioner might have needed a special diet for recovery.
Thus, I deem it fit to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner towards special diet.

21. Though no cogent evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment, it cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner might have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities at least for some months,
and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
8 doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- as attendant charges.

22. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- (30,000+50,000 + 40,000)
under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :-
23.

In her examination-in-chief Ex. PW1/A tendered on 30.05.2022 by way of affidavit attested on 31.01.2018, petitioner deposed that she is an MBA and at the time of accident, she was working with Parcel Now World Wide, a logistic startup and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to permanent disability sustained in the accident, she would not be able to get job in the same way as prior to the accident and she is unable to resume her job.

During her cross-examination, she stated that she had worked for 06 months in the above-stated company prior to the accident and further that she joined her service after the accident in September 2019 in another company namely Aquagiri Processing Pvt. Ltd.
Ld. Counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner could not work for 22 months due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
However, this claim is not substantiated through medical record or even through the testimony of petitioner.
It is an admitted case she was never thrown out of job and instead during the period of her treatment itself, the company where she was working had been shut down.
Hence, there is no question of her re-joining the same job.

There is nothing in the shape of medical documents to show that she was unable to take up new employment till September 2019 or that she made an effort to take up new job but due to the injuries sustained by her, she was declined a suitable job.

However, considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the continuous treatment and admission in hospital and further the long period of treatment, it can reasonably be assumed that she remained unable to work for about 10 months from the date of accident.

She was getting salary of Rs.39,800/- per month on the date of accident and hence, on account of loss of income, an amount of Rs. 3,98,000/- (39,800 X10) is being awarded as compensation under this head.

LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY :
24.
The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.
In case bearing citation Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Arising out of civil appeal No. 8918 of 2010, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that :-
10.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claim could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether ; (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
9 kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether inspite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of the claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or disablement may be around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver of a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be 100%, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant is clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could performed his clerical functions,
in that even the loss of earnings capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter nor 60% which is the actual physical disability but far less.

In fact, there may not be need to award any compensation under the head of 'Loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in Government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities on the consequences of losing his hand....."

25. The disability certificate of LBS Hospital clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 93%
disability in relation to right upper limb.
The doctor has been examined as PW2.
PW2 Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir has deposed that petitioner suffered permanent disability to the extent of 93% in relation to right upper limb and disability certificate Ex.PW2/A was issued in this regard.
The petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.
PW2 did not state a word to suggest what hindrance would be faced or has been faced by the petitioner in taking up any job in future and how her prospects would be marred.
Petitioner has claimed to be working at the time of accident and as per her Aadhar Card, she was only about 26 years 5 months and 24 days of age on that day.
She has not explained as to in what manner she shall not be able to work as per her ability and qualification.

However, considering that petitioner was a young woman at the time of accident and claimed to be employed at that time and also considering that her right hand which is stated to be her dominant hand, has suffered from near total amputation, it can be assumed that the permanent disability was of the nature as might have hampered her future prospects and the nature of job she could take up must have been rendered limited to a considerable extent, post her accident.

It is mentioned in her testimony during cross-examination that she did not resign from her previous job and was not even terminated but the said company was closed down in January 2017 or January 2018.
She deposed in her cross-examination dated 30.05.2022 that she was getting salary of Rs.60,000/- as on the date of cross-examination dated 30.05.2022 while working in Aquagiri processing Pvt. Ltd.

However,
during her further cross-examination on 18.01.2023, she produced her bank statement Ex.PW1/9 &
Ex. PW1/10 and stated clearly that in September 2019 she joined new company Aquagiri and was getting salary of Rs.47,067/- per month as on date.

It is interesting to note that though she has filed on record her bank statement, she has not filed relevant part of bank statement for year 2022 which could reflect the salary being fetched by her in May 2022 or prior to it.

There is no claim made by the petitioner that her salary had been decreased from Rs.60,000/- to Rs. 47,067/- over a period of time and hence no observation or conclusion can be arrived at by the Tribunal in that regard.

The Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
10

documents placed on record together with the testimony of the petitioner do not reflect any diminished salary post accident and there is nothing in her testimony to suggest that on account of the accident, there was any change in her job profile or reduction of income or that there has been any loss of job prospects.

The bank statement of year 2019 reflects that she received Rs.47,067/-
from her employer as salary as on 06.09.2019 and further the said amount was consistently received by her in the year 2019.

Petitioner has not averred a word to suggest the nature of work done by her at work place and whether the was sitting or desk job or involved any active and consistent participation of use of her right upper limb, which was rendered incapable of use due to permanent disability suffered by her or that due to this, she lost any good opportunity to work or get any promotion at her present work place, despite her educational qualification and mental capability.
No evidence has been led by the petitioner even to suggest that her job profile requires active and consistent use of computer or any other technological device requiring active use of right hand.
She has not led any evidence even to suggest that her right hand is dominant hand or whether or not she has acquired the tact and expertise in use of non-dominant hand in her work sphere.
On query of the Tribunal made during final arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioner submitted that right hand of petitioner was her dominant hand.
There is no evidence led by the petitioner to suggest that her earlier job profile and pay scale was superior to the subsequent job taken by her post accident.

At the same time, it cannot be lost sight of that petitioner is in a private job and due to permanent disability sustained by her, she might have suffered from loss of income as her career prospect definitely should have been marred and even in future she might face further difficulty on account of it.
Hence, a balanced approach has to be taken by the Tribunal.

Therefore, I am of the opinion that functional disability in relation to right lower limb of the petitioner must be considered as 30% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

26. The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows the date of birth of petitioner as 05.03.1991,
which would mean that she was around 26 years 5 months of age at the time of accident and thus,
multiplier of 17 would be applicable.

Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40 % has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was less than 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors.,
2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court).

There is no evidence led by the petitioner to suggest that the longevity of petitioner has been adversely affected due to the accident in question or that petitioner had any particular dream for future, which is shattered due to accident and there is absolutely no evidence to show any loss of expectation of life.

During oral argument addressed, it was stated by Ld. LIABILITY:
30.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured i.e.
the owner-cum-driver of Hydra Crane No. HR-55V-4780, the Insurance company/IFFCO TOKIO GIC is liable to compensate the third party.

The insurance company has examined a witness R3W1 to prove the objections raised by it and to prove that term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident as his driving licence did not have any endorsement for driving of crane, a special vehicle and further that there was no permit and fitness certificate of offending vehicle.

It is not disputed that R1 did not have a valid permit to drive the crane in NCT of Delhi and had a local permit of Haryana and further that the offending vehicle Hydra Crane No.

sentences.text: In my considered view, crane is a special vehicle and fitness of a crane should be ensured before driving such a special vehicle with a view to avoid any mishap.
In the case at hand, the mechanical defect in the crane is apparent.

Though R1 claimed in his cross-examination that Haryana Government stopped issuing fitness certificate to cranes before the date of accident and that no permit is required to drive a crane in Delhi, he did not lead any evidence to suggest that category D Vehicle registered in Haryana could be plied on public road in Delhi without fitness certificate.
R3W1 deposed that R1 did not have endorsement to drive a crane on his driving licence on the date of accident and the same was a requirement.

No suggestion was given to R3W1 that despite the offending vehicle in question being a category D vehicle with term excavator mentioned on the insurance certificate, still driver did not require an endorsement on the licence, giving authority to the driver to drive a crane.
Further, offending vehicle did not have a permit to be taken to Delhi and was registered in Haryana, with a Haryana permit.
R1 failed to lead any evidence to suggest that permit was not required for a crane in Delhi but required in Haryana.

Hence, in my considered view, R3 has been successful in proving that the insured vehicle was used/plight without valid permit, valid driving licence and fitness certificate and hence, there was breach of general terms and conditions of insurance policy.
However, the breach in question is not such as would affect the right of third party, once it is established that vehicle was covered under the policy of insurance.
Law is well settled that insurance company would be entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the registered owner/insured of the offending vehicle.

In case titled as Gurmeet Singh vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors, MAC App 288/2021 decided on 06.10.2023, it has been held that the respondent no. 3/ insurer is entitled to recover the compensation amount paid to the claimants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, insurance company is entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the respondent No.1 after paying the aforesaid compensation to the petitioner in the first place.

In view of above, it is held that respondent no.3/
insurer shall be liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

RELIEF:
31.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.62,10,000/- (Rupees Sixty Two Lakhs Ten Thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3/ insurer, which shall be recoverable by the insurance company from the respondent No.1.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
32. With these observations, the present claim petition is disposed off.
33. File be consigned to Record Room.

Arising out of civil appeal No. 8918 of 2010, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that :-
10.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claim could carry on inspite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether ; (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/
9 kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether inspite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
In the absence of anything to suggest that while acting in tandem during carrying of the slab together fastened onto their lifting parts, hydra crane bearing No.
HR-99X-BT4138 was operated in such a manner as resulting in the losing of balance by the hydra crane HR-55V-4780, it cannot automatically be deduced that the driver of the said crane attributed to the accident by any of his rash or negligent conduct.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
No evidence was led by any of the respondents in their defence and R1 did not enter into witness box to assail the claim of the petitioner.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though she may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
United India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Patrica Jean Mahajan & Ors. of Supreme Court of India in Appeal (Civil) 3655-58 of 2002; and Mrs. Helen C. Rebello & Ors. Vs.
